messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>

Date: 2029-10-28T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: BridgePoint late-stage sizing — can you run a quick availability check?

Karthik —

BridgePoint just moved to legal and wants a short window to lock in dedicated capacity if we can guarantee runway for Q1 onboarding. Quick asks: can you confirm current dedicated pool headroom for us-east (NVIDIA H100 equivalent) and what a provisional 90-day soft-hold would look like (GPU count and skus)?

Ben, looping you for ops implications if Karthik recommends a soft-hold.

High level expected workload from the customer (sourced from Alex):
- Peak concurrent workers: 60
- Model family: Llama-3-style 70B (we're recommending a quantized variant)
- Typical sequence length: 1024 tokens
- Target p99 latency: <= 350ms (token streaming)

They asked for a cost-aware plan and a fallback to smaller quantized models if needed. I can push for a 30% acceptance buffer in the commercial terms if that helps.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-10-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BridgePoint late-stage sizing — can you run a quick availability check?

Vanessa / Ben —

Thanks for the heads-up. I pulled a quick inventory snapshot for us-east (H100-class pool):
- Total H100-equivalent committed to Dedicated customers: 1,280 GPUs
- Current reserved (long-term reserved + Dedicated customers): 1,060 GPUs
- Short-term buffer / available for provisional holds: ~220 GPUs (subject to scheduled maint windows in Nov)

Given BridgePoint's expected concurrency (60 workers) and model choice (70B quantized), rough sizing assumptions: ~3 GPUs per worker for steady-state inference when using optimized batching (conservative) => ~180 GPUs sustained. For peak bursts with headroom for A/B and rollout, add ~30% => ~234 GPUs.

Options to present:
1) 90-day soft-hold: allocate 250 GPUs from short-term buffer; no immediate charge, but a commercial clause to convert to reserved capacity if used >30 days.
2) Conditional hold with time-bound escrow: reserve 180 GPUs guaranteed, additional 74 GPUs on-demand with preemptible pricing when used.
3) No hold, but priority routing + autoscaling policy that pins them to a mix of H100 + quantized H100 variants (cost savings, faster ramp).

Questions I need from BridgePoint to finalize:
- Expected steady-state vs peak day ratio (hours per day at peak)
- Whether they require data-plane isolation (Dedicated pool vs Dedicated + VPC) — drives provisioning time
- Signed PoC start date window (they mentioned early Jan)

If we go with option 1 or 2 I recommend we create a provisional ticket and tag 250 GPUs in the pool; Ben, can you confirm the operational steps and ETA to mark a soft-hold in the system (and any scheduled maintenance that would reduce the 220 buffer)? Rishi, please note potential infra constraints — we may need to pre-stage model quantized variants to reduce memory footprint.

I'll draft a short internal note to lock the provisional hold once we get BridgePoint's steady/peak split and confirm their PoC start date.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Capacity Planner, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@bridgepoint.ai>

Date: 2029-10-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RE: BridgePoint late-stage sizing — can you run a quick availability check?

Karthik / Vanessa —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from our side (attached is the completed capacity spec and draft SOW):
- Steady-state: expect ~40 active workers for 16 hours/day (training/eval windows outside this)
- Peak window: 4 hours/day with 60 workers, 1–2 peak days/week during initial onboarding
- Isolation: prefer Dedicated pool (no VPC) for now, but we need HIPAA controls on logs (we'll follow up with a security questionnaire)
- PoC target start: 2029-01-15 with a 6-week onboarding sprint

On their ask for fallback: we are open to quantized variants if you can guarantee functional parity and tight latency bounds. Cost exposure must be capped for the PoC.

We'll sign a provisional MOU if you can provide a 90-day soft-hold guarantee and a clear conversion trigger.

Alex Chen
Head of ML, BridgePoint AI
alex.chen@bridgepoint.ai

Subject: BridgePoint provisional hold authorization (internal)

Team —

Per Alex's confirmation and the attached SOW, BridgePoint is asking for a 90-day soft-hold to guarantee runway for their PoC starting 2029-01-15. Based on the specifics they provided I recommend we proceed with Option 1 (provisional 250 GPU soft-hold) with the following guardrails: 

Action items / notes:
- Ben: please open provisional hold ticket PH-20291101-BP and tag 250 H100-equivalent GPUs in us-east pool. Provide ETA for hold activation and note any maintenance windows that could affect availability (we're currently showing a small maintenance window on 2029-11-14 which would reduce buffer by ~20 GPUs).
- Rishi: pre-stage quantized 70B variant and validate p99 latency target on a 16-worker sim (reference test harness: /ops/test-harness/bench-70b). If latency regression >15% on quantized variant, escalate and propose alternate routing.
- Vanessa: include a conversion clause in the provisional MOU: convert soft-hold to reserved capacity if BridgePoint consumes >45% of hold for more than 30 consecutive days. Legal should sign off on language.
- Ops: set billing stub for provisional hold (no invoicing unless converted) and add a monitoring dashboard (cost + p99 latency) accessible to account team and customer.

Rationale: the pool buffer is tight but the 250 GPU hold is within feasible limits if we accept a small reduction in on-demand buffer for November. This balances commercial flexibility for the customer with our operational runway.

I'll create the provisional ticket and update the HubSpot deal record with the hold details after Ben confirms ETA.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Capacity Planner, Redwood Inference
